chunks.text: Diabetes occurs when your blood glucose, also called blood sugar, is too high.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Condition

chunks.text: High blood glucose can cause health problems over time.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Condition

chunks.text: The main types of diabetes are type 1, type 2, and gestational.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Condition

chunks.text: Increased thirst and urination, feeling tired, unexplained weight loss, and blurred vision are symptoms of diabetes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Symptom

chunks.text: Many people have no symptoms and don’t know they have diabetes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Symptom

chunks.text: Each type of diabetes has different causes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Symptom

chunks.text: You are more likely to develop type 2 diabetes if you have a family history of diabetes, are overweight or have obesity, or are 35 or older.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: RiskFactor

chunks.text: Physical inactivity, race, ethnicity, and certain health problems also affect your chances of developing type 2 diabetes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: RiskFactor

chunks.text: A history of gestational diabetes is a risk factor for the parent and the child.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: RiskFactor

chunks.text: You can prevent or delay type 2 diabetes by losing weight if you are overweight, being active for 30 minutes most days of the week, and following a reduced-calorie eating plan.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: EducationalAction

chunks.text: Doctors use a variety of tests to diagnose diabetes and prediabetes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: DiagnosticTest

chunks.text: Your doctor may recommend different tests depending on whether you have symptoms or not, or whether you are pregnant.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: DiagnosticTest

chunks.text: Managing your diabetes means managing your blood glucose, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: EducationalAction

chunks.text: Work with your health care team to create a diabetes care plan that works for you.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: EducationalAction

chunks.text: Your diabetes meal plan helps you manage your blood glucose.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: LifestyleTopic

chunks.text: Moderate physical activity most days of the week also helps control blood glucose.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: LifestyleTopic

chunks.text: Talk with your health care team about a plan for eating and physical activity that is right for you.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: LifestyleTopic

chunks.text: Learn more about less-common types of diabetes.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
chunks.usage_notes: NIDDK copyright policy: majority copyright free; text only, no logos/images/third-party material. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/copyright
chunks.label: Condition

chunks.text: If you have diabetes and plan to get pregnant, or develop diabetes during pregnancy, you can take steps to keep yourself and your baby healthy.
chunks.title: Diabetes Overview
